result: {"self_assessment": "Impact: I built the bottom body line of the fish (stroke 2), branching off the nose. It was connected to the start and live all the way to the crossing, so the lower half of the outline falls. In the last stretch I took on the fork's inner notch, which defines the forked tail. I laid the upper notch join and was partway through the lower one when time was called. Honestly, I can't confirm the notch closed fully, so the tail fork may read less crisply than intended. The body and both tail pieces were live, and about 199 of 248 dominoes were connected to the start at the last check. Execution: My line went down cleanly and stayed connected to the start. I joined my line to Leo's coming from the tail. I told him to stand up the dominoes his bump had knocked down before he laid the join. I also took on the notch join myself so two people wouldn't bump each other there. Where I fell short: the table ran out of dominoes, I spent the final minutes on a small fiddly piece, and the lower notch join was still in progress at the push. I should have asked for spare dominoes earlier. Collaboration: I kept my status updates short and specific, said where my line ended so Leo and I could meet in the middle, and asked others to stay off the notch to avoid bumps. I asked Priya, Leo and Tom to lift stray pale dominoes so the pile refilled, and all three did. Leadership: Priya set the plan, and I backed it rather than relitigating it. I gave a clear status update to the whole table at the halfway point and took ownership of the open notch instead of leaving it unclaimed. Next time I'd flag supply risk sooner and prioritise the joins that most affect whether the animal is recognisable."}
